rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The tanwīn in ghulām magnifies the expression, fitting Joseph, whom the author says was among the most handsome boys.
rows.anchor: والظاهر أن التنوين فيه للتفخيم وحق له ذلك فقد كان عليه من أحسن الغلمان

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: Al-Baghawī cites a Prophetic report that Joseph was given half of beauty; no grading is stated.
rows.anchor: وذكر البغوي عنه صلى الله تعالى عليه وسلم أنه قال : أعطي يوسف شطر الحسن

rows.speaker: محمد بن إسحاق
rows.claim: Ibn Isḥāq says Joseph and his mother possessed two-thirds of beauty.
rows.anchor: وقال محمد بن إسحاق : ذهب يوسف وأمه بثلثي الحسن

rows.speaker: كعب الأحبار
rows.claim: Al-Thaʿlabī transmits Kaʿb's elaborate description of Joseph's handsome face, hair, eyes, complexion, smile, and exceptional beauty.
rows.anchor: وحكى الثعلبي عن كعب الأحبار أنه قال : كان يوسف حسن الوجه جعد الشعر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A story says the sides of the well wept when Joseph was brought out; the author compares this to saying a house wept at someone's loss.
rows.anchor: ويحكى أن جوانب الجب بكت عليه حين خرج منها ولعله من باب بكت الدار لفقد فلان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The water-drawer likely exclaimed that he had found a boy as soon as he saw Joseph.
rows.anchor: قول الوارد ( يا بشرى هذا غلام ) كان عند رؤيته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One reading takes they concealed him as the water-drawer and companions hiding Joseph from the caravan lest its members want him.
rows.anchor: أي أخفاه الوارد وأصحابه عن بقية الرفقة حتى لا تراه فتطمع فيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another reading says the party concealed how Joseph was found in the well, claiming the people at the water handed him over for sale in Egypt.
rows.anchor: وقيل : أخفوا أمره وكونه وجد في البئر وقالوا لسائر القافلة : دفعه إلينا أهل الماء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A further interpretation makes the concealed party Joseph's brothers: one returned, saw him with the caravan, and the brothers claimed he was their runaway slave.
rows.anchor: وقيل : الضمير لإخوة يوسف وذلك أن بعضهم رجع ليتحقق أمره فرآه عند السيارة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Joseph stayed silent for fear they would kill him; one report says the brothers threatened him in Hebrew and he acknowledged enslavement before they bought him.
rows.anchor: وسكت يوسف مخافة أن يقتلوه وفي رواية أنهم قالوا بالعبرانية : لا تنكر العبودية نقتلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A variant says Judah, who brought Joseph food, found him missing from the well and informed his brothers.
rows.anchor: وقيل : كان يهوذا يأتيه الطعام فأتاه يوم أخرج فلم يجده في الجب

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās is reported to support identifying the concealed party as the brothers; the author notes this fits the singular said, plural concealed, and coming threat.
rows.anchor: وروي كون الضمير للأخوة عن ابن عباس رضي الله تعالى عنهما قيل : وهو المناسب لإفراد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The brothers reading creates no syntactic disorder, but the apparent reading remains that the water-drawer and companions hid Joseph.
rows.anchor: وليس فيه اختلال في النظم ولا يخفى أن الظاهر ما أشير إليه أولا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Bidāʿatan is accusative as a circumstantial expression: they concealed Joseph while treating him as trade merchandise.
rows.anchor: ونصب قوله سبحانه : بضاعة ( على الحال أي أخفوه حال كونه متاعا للتجارة

rows.speaker: الفرائد
rows.claim: Al-Farāʾid says asarrūhu carries the sense of making Joseph merchandise, with Joseph as its object.
rows.anchor: وفي الفرائد أنه ضمن أسروه معنى جعلوه أي جعلوه بضاعة

rows.speaker: ابن الحاجب
rows.claim: Ibn al-Ḥājib allows bidāʿatan as a purpose object because the concealers and purpose-seeking agents are the same: they hid Joseph to obtain money from him.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن الحاجب : يحتمل أن يكون مفعولا له أي لأجل التجارة وليس شرطه مفقودا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Bidāʿatan cannot be a specification; it derives from cutting or dividing, like a portion of property set aside for trade.
rows.anchor: ولا يجوز أن يكون تمييزا وهو من البضع بمعنى القطع وكأن البضاعة إنما سميت بذلك

rows.speaker: الراغب
rows.claim: Al-Rāghib requires bidāʿa to be a substantial portion of wealth, a qualification most lexicographers do not require.
rows.anchor: وإعتبر الراغب في البضاعة كونها قطعة وافرة من المال تقتنى للتجارة ولم يعتبر الكثير كونها وافرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God knew their secret actions; the warning especially threatens Joseph's brothers for wronging their father and brother and exposing Joseph to the indignity of sale.
rows.anchor: وصرح غير واحد أن هذا وعيد لإخوة يوسف عليه السلام على ما صنعوا بأبيهم وأخيهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The subject of sh rawhu may be the brothers, with shara meaning sold, or the caravan, with it meaning bought; the caravan could have bought Joseph among themselves before selling him.
rows.anchor: الضمير المرفوع إما للأخوة فشري بمعنى باع وإما للسيارة فهو بمعنى اشترى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Two cited poems attest shara meaning bought: one describes buying a cloak after Bard, another buying Abū Zayd with all one's property.
rows.anchor: كما في قوله : ( وشريت ) بردا ليتني من بعد برد كنت هامه وقوله ولو أن هذا الموت يقبل فدية ( شريت ) أبا زيد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Bakhs is deficiency used as a passive participle; al-Rāghib instead allows an obviously underpriced sale.
rows.anchor: أي نقص وهو مصدر أريد به اسم المفعول أي منقوص وجوز الراغب أن يكون بمعنى باخس

rows.speaker: مقاتل
rows.claim: Muqātil glosses bakhs as counterfeit and deficient in assay.
rows.anchor: وقال مقاتل : زيف ناقص العيار

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatāda calls the price unjust because Joseph was wronged in the sale.
rows.anchor: وقال قتادة : بخس ظلم لأنه ظلموه في بيعه

rows.speaker: ابن عباس والضحاك
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās, al-Ḍaḥḥāk, and others say the price was unlawful because it was payment for a free person; unlawful wealth is deficient in blessing.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن عباس والضحاك في آخرين : البخس الحرام وكان ذلك حراما لأنه ثمن الحر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Dirham is an appositive specifying the price; counted coins imply a small amount because large sums were ordinarily weighed.
rows.anchor: ( درهم ( بدل من ثمن أي لا دنانير معدودة ( أي قليلة وكني بالعد عن القلة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Most reports count twenty dirhams; Ibn ʿAbbās reports twenty-two. Other reports give twenty plus a cloak and shoes, thirty plus clothing and shoes, eighteen for footwear, or ten.
rows.anchor: وكانت عدة هذه الدراهم في كثير من الروايات عشرين درهما وفي رواية عن ابن عباس اثنين وعشرين

rows.speaker: عكرمة
rows.claim: ʿIkrima reports forty dirhams; this fits the custom of weighing only sums reaching forty because forty could still be counted.
rows.anchor: وعن عكرمة أنها كانت أربعين درهما ولا يأبى هذا ما ذكره غير واحد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase means they were disinclined toward Joseph, its apparent antecedent; if they are the brothers, they are the sellers.
rows.anchor: ( وكانوا فيه ( أي في يوسف كما هو الظاهر ( من الزاهدين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Zāhidīn means disinclined; if the caravan sold Joseph, they were casual about a found object and feared a claimant, so they sold to the first bidder cheaply.
rows.anchor: أي الراغبين عنه والضمير في ( وكانوا ) إن كان للإخوة فظاهر وإن كان للرفقة وكانوا بائعين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If the caravan had bought him from one another or the brothers, they were wary because they thought he was a runaway and feared risking their money.
rows.anchor: فزهدهم لأنهم إعتقدوا فيه أنه آبق فخافوا أن يخاطروا بما لهم فيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another interpretation makes fīhi refer to the price, which they disdained for poor quality or because they only wanted Joseph gone.
rows.anchor: وقيل : ضمير ( فيه ) للثمن وزهدهم فيه لرداءته أو لأن مقصودهم ليس إلا إبعاد يوسف

rows.speaker: ابن مالك
rows.claim: Ibn Mālik attaches min al-zāhidīn to an implicit adjective indicated by the expressed word, since the relative clause of al cannot normally affect an earlier phrase.
rows.anchor: والجار على ما نقل عن ابن مالك متعلق بمحذوف يدل عليه الزاهدين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On that analysis min al-zāhidīn may reinforce or explain the omitted adjective, or act as a second predicate; it cannot be a substitute because it contains min.
rows.anchor: وهل ( من الزاهدين ) حينئذ صفة لزاهدين المحذوف مؤكدة كما نقول : عالم من العلماء

rows.speaker: ابن الحاجب
rows.claim: Ibn al-Ḥājib attaches the phrase directly to the relative clause; al differs from other relative particles and permits its complement to precede it.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن الحاجب في أماليه : إنه متعلق بالصلة والمعنى عليه بلا شبهة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A later objection about an unsupported active participle is misplaced: the dispute concerns direct subjects and objects, while prepositional phrases retain verbal force readily.
rows.anchor: لأن محل محل الخلاف عمله في الفاعل والمفعول به الصريح لا في الجار والمجرور

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some grammarians say the adjective relies on kāna's noun, originally a subject; al-Raḍī recognizes reliance on a subject in its current or original position.
rows.anchor: وقال بعض المتأخرين : إن الصفة هنا معتمدة على اسم كانوا وهو مبتدأ في الأصل

rows.speaker: الرضي
rows.claim: Al-Raḍī says reliance on the adjective's subject can hold when it is a present or former subject.
rows.anchor: ففي الرضي عند قول ابن الحاجب : والإعتماد على صاحبه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some appeal to the greater syntactic latitude of adverbs and prepositional phrases; the common view is that Joseph's brothers sold him and disdained him.
rows.anchor: ومن الناس من يتمسك بعموم يتوسع في الظرف والججار والمجرور ما لا يتوسع في غيرهما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A report begins that, when selling Joseph, the brothers told the merchant he was a runaway thief.
rows.anchor: والشائع أن الباعة إخوته والزاهدين هم وفي بعض الآثار أنهم حين باعوه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In a report the brothers called Joseph a runaway thief; the merchant bound and guarded him with a black enslaved man.
rows.anchor: قالوا للتاجر : إنه لص آبق فقيده ووكل به عبدا أسود

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Joseph wept as the caravan departed and asked to bid farewell; the merchant sent him with the guard, who admired Joseph's kindness and the brothers' harshness.
rows.anchor: فقال : أريد أن أصل إلى الذين باعوني لأودعهم وأسلم عليهم سلام من لا يرجع إليهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Joseph kissed and embraced each brother, praying for their protection and mercy despite their betrayal.
rows.anchor: فجعل يوسف ينكب على كل واحد منهم ويقبله ويعانقه ويقول : حفظكم الله تعالى وإن ضيعتموني

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The story says the sheep miscarried from the distress of Joseph's farewell.
rows.anchor: قيل : إن الأغنام ألقت ما في بطونها من هول هذا التوديع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On the journey Joseph saw his mother Rachel's grave, embraced it, and lamented that his brothers had cast him into the well and sold him cheaply.
rows.anchor: مر بقبر أمه راحيل في مقابر كنعان فلما أبصر القبر لم يتمالك أن رمى بنفسه عليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The guard mistook Joseph's absence for escape and struck him; Joseph explained it was his mother's grave and promised not to repeat the delay.
rows.anchor: ثم لطمه لطمة شديدة فغشي عليه ثم أفاق فقال له : لا تؤاخذني هذا قبر أمي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Joseph prayed by the honor of Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob that God forgive him; angels interceded, and God sent Gabriel to comfort him.
rows.anchor: فضجت الملائكة إلى الله تعالى عند ذلك فقال تبارك وتعالى : يا ملائكتي هذا نبيي وابن أنبيائي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Gabriel said Joseph's grief had made the angels of the seven heavens weep; Joseph asked him to treat God's creatures gently because God is patient.
rows.anchor: فقال : يا صديق الله ربك يقرئك السلام ويقول لك : مهلا عليك فقد أبكيت ملائكة السماوات السبع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After the guard confessed, the merchant offered himself for retaliation; Joseph forgave them, saying his family pardons when wronged, and the storm cleared.
rows.anchor: فقال يوسف : ما أنا من قوم إذا ظلموا يقتصون ولكني من أهل بيت إذ ظلموا عفوا وغفروا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The merchant who brought Joseph from the well was said to be Mālik ibn Dhʿar, though another identity is also reported.
rows.anchor: وكان هذا التاجر فيما قيل : مالك بن ذعر الذي أخرجه من الجب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A report says the Egyptian buyer later sold Joseph for twenty dinars, a pair of shoes, and two white garments; another says bidding reached his weight in musk, silver, and silk before the Aziz bought him.
rows.anchor: وروي أنه حين ورد به مصر باعه بعشرين دينارا وزوجي نعل وثوبين أبيضين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Other identifications call the buyer the royal baker, cupbearer, keeper of animals, or famous prison warden; the relied-upon view is the Aziz, named Quṭayfir, Aṭfīr, or Qanṭūrā, first reported from Ibn ʿAbbās.
rows.anchor: وقيل : كان خباز الملك وصاحب شرابه ودوابه وصاحب السجن المشهور والمعول عليه هو الأول واسمه قطفير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This Egyptian purchase differs from the earlier cheap sale; equating them is very weak because it leaves from Egypt with little purpose.
rows.anchor: فهذا الشراء غير الشراء السابق الذي كان بثمن بخس وزعم اتحادهما ضعيف جدا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The king was reportedly Rayyān ibn al-Walīd al-ʿAmalīqī; he believed in Joseph before dying, and his successor Qābūs ibn Muṣʿab refused Joseph's call to faith.
rows.anchor: وكان الملك يومئذ الريان بن الوليد العمليقي ومات في حياة يوسف عليه السلام بعد أن آمن به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One view says Moses' Pharaoh ruled in Joseph's time and lived four hundred years, citing 40:34; another says Moses' Pharaoh descended from Joseph's Pharaoh, which the author calls correct.
rows.anchor: وقيل : فرعون موسى عليه السلام من أولاد فرعون يوسف عليه السلام والآية من قبيل خطاب الأولاد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Aziz appears to have been an unbeliever, supported by reports that an idol stood in his house.
rows.anchor: وظاهر أمر العزيز أنه كان كافرا

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujāhid says the Aziz was a believer; the author suggests he may mean later belief, since belief when Joseph was purchased is hardly acceptable.
rows.anchor: وقال مجاهد : كان مؤمنا ولعل مراده أنه آمن بعد ذاك

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujāhid's report names the Aziz's wife Rāʿīl daughter of Raʿābīl; al-Suddī names her Zulaykhā daughter of Tamlikhā, with other reports reversing name and nickname.
rows.anchor: راعيل ( 1 ) بنت رعابيل وهو المروي عن مجاهد

rows.speaker: السدي
rows.claim: Al-Suddī's report gives the wife's name as Zulaykhā; other accounts call her Rāʿīl nicknamed Zulaykhā or vice versa.
rows.anchor: وقال السدي : زليخا ( 2 ) بنت تمليخا وقيل : اسمها راعيل ولقبها زليخا

rows.speaker: أبو البقاء
rows.claim: Abū al-Baqāʾ says min Miṣr attaches to ishtarāhu, like buying from Baghdad, or describes the buyer as Egyptian; the second prepositional phrase attaches to qāla.
rows.anchor: والجار الأول كما قال أبو البقاء : متعلق باشتراه كقولك اشتريته من بغداد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Akramī mathwāhu means make his lodging pleasant; honoring the place is a metonym for honoring Joseph fully, though mathwā may be an expendable word for caring for him as a guest.
rows.anchor: مقول القول : ( أكرمي مثوه ( أي اجعلي محل ثوائه وإقامته كريما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: May he benefit us means Joseph may help with household needs after learning how affairs work; taking him as a son means adoption, and reports say the Aziz was infertile.
rows.anchor: ( عسى أن ينفعنا ( في قضاء مصالحنا إذا تدرب في الأمور وعرف مجاريها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The proposal that aw prevents combining both options, meaning they might sell Joseph for profit, is unsound; the Aziz spoke because Joseph showed signs of intelligence and promise.
rows.anchor: وزعم بعضهم أنه لمنع الجمع على معنى عسى أن نبيعه فننتفع بثمنه وليس بشيء

rows.speaker: ابن مسعود
rows.claim: Ibn Masʿūd, transmitted by Saʿīd ibn Manṣūr, al-Ḥākim (who authenticated it), and others, names three perceptive people: the Aziz about Joseph, the woman who hired Moses, and Abū Bakr appointing ʿUmar.
rows.anchor: قال ابن مسعود رضي الله تعالى عنه فيما أخرجه سعيد بن منصور والحاكم وصححه وجماعة : أفرس الناس ثلاثة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Making Joseph established in the land means granting him a place or position; the related verbs are close in use but differ between fixing someone in a place and providing him a place.
rows.anchor: أي جعلنا له فيها مكانا يقال : مكنه فيه أي أثبته فيه ومكن له فيه أي جعل له مكانا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Here place means status, not mere physical location; the verse's comparison may recall Joseph's fine lodging in the Aziz's house or heart and God's granting him high standing in Egypt.
rows.anchor: والمراد بالمكان هنا المكانة والمنزلة لا البعد المجرد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some explain establishment as making Joseph prominent among Egyptians and beloved in their hearts; the reference may be to the prior source or the following verb, with the kāf emphasizing its greatness.
rows.anchor: وفسر الجعل المذكور بجعله وجيها فيما بين أهل مصر ومحببا في قلوبهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A scholar's comparison invokes God's making the community a balanced nation; here the reference may be empowerment in the Aziz's heart or home.
rows.anchor: على ما ذكروا في ( وكذلك جعلناكم أمة وسطا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The apparent meaning is that Joseph became a ruler able to command Egypt; making dream interpretation the purpose is difficult because it follows from empowerment, unless teaching means applying divine books and prophetic practice in just rule.
rows.anchor: ولعل الظاهر حمله على جعله ملكا يتصرف في أرض مصر بالأمر والنهي إلا أن في جعل التعليم المذكور غاية له خفاء

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujāhid explains teaching taʾwīl al-aḥādīth as dream interpretation, especially the king's and two prison companions' dreams; Joseph says this is part of what his Lord taught him.
rows.anchor: ولنعلمه من تأويل الأحاديث ( أي بعض تعبير الرؤيا التي عمدتها رؤيا الملك وصاحبي السجن وروي هذا المعنى عن مجاهد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another interpretation is that God taught Joseph the secrets of divine books and the practices of earlier prophets so he could rule justly and guide people in each case.
rows.anchor: أراد بتعليم تأويل الأحاديث تفهيم غوامض أسرار الكتب الإلهية ودقائق سنن الأنبياء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Allah prevails over His affair: nothing prevents or contests His will, and His command occurs by His saying Be, and it is.
rows.anchor: لا يمنع عما يشاء ولا ينازع فيما يريد بل إنما أمره لشيء إذا أراد أن يقول له كن فيكون

rows.speaker: ابن جبير
rows.claim: Ibn Jubayr takes the pronoun in His affair as referring to God; al-Quṭrubī instead refers it to Joseph, whom God personally directs and does not leave to others.
rows.anchor: وإلى رجوع ضمير أمره إلى الله تعالى ذهب ابن جبير

rows.speaker: القطربي
rows.claim: Al-Quṭrubī's reading makes God the one who carefully governs Joseph; under either reading, the brothers' and the Aziz's wife's schemes cannot prevail.
rows.anchor: وإلى رجوعه إلى يوسف عليه السلام ذهب القطربي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author says the God-referent reading supports Sunni doctrine and recalls the verse that falsehood vanishes; most people fail to know God's complete control.
rows.anchor: والآية على الأول صريحة في مذهب أهل السنة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Poetic sayings illustrate that when God's river flows, another river is swept away and the brothers' schemes cannot prevail.
rows.anchor: وإذا جاء نهر الله تعالى بطل نهر معقل فأين يقع كيد الإخوة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: People wrongly suppose they control what they do and leave, though all affairs belong to God; they fail to perceive His subtle planning and hidden favor.
rows.anchor: زعما منهم أن لهم من الأمر شيئا وأنى لهم ذلك وأن الأمر كله لله عز وجل

rows.speaker: ابن عطية
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAṭiyya says most people refers to unbelievers; other views specify Egyptians or Meccans, or use it to mean everyone unable to know God's unseen.
rows.anchor: والمراد بأكثر الناس قيل : الكفار ونقل ذلك عن ابن عطية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author keeps the ordinary sense of most people and includes anyone lacking knowledge of the matters just described, possibly including Muʿtazilites.
rows.anchor: والأولى أن يبقى على ما يتبادر منه ولا يقتصر في تفسيره على ما تضمنته الأقوال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ashudd marks the end of bodily growth and strength, commonly between thirty and forty; some set its maximum at sixty-two, while Abū ʿUbayda and reliable linguists make it the end of youth before decline.
rows.anchor: أي بلغ زمان إنتهاء اشتداد جسمه وقوته وهو سن الوقوف عن النمو المعتد به أعني ما بين الثلاثين

rows.speaker: مهذب الدين محمد بن علي الخيمي
rows.claim: The grammarian Muhadhdhib al-Dīn al-Khaymī gives thirty-five years, completed at forty.
rows.anchor: وسئل القاضي النحوي مهذب الدين محمد بن علي بن علي بن أبي طالب الخيمي عنه فقال : هو خمس وثلاثون سنة

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: Al-Zajjāj places ashudd from seventeen years until around forty.
rows.anchor: وقال الزجاج : هو سبعة عشر عاما إلى نحو الأربعين

rows.speaker: مجاهد وقتادة وابن عباس
rows.claim: Reports from Mujāhid and Qatāda relayed by Ibn Jubayr from Ibn ʿAbbās give thirty-three, thirty, or twenty-one years.
rows.anchor: وعن مجاهد وقتادة ورواه ابن جبير عن ابن عباس أنه ثلاثة وثلاثون أو ثلاثون أو أحد وعشرون

rows.speaker: الضحاك
rows.claim: Al-Ḍaḥḥāk says ashudd is twenty years.
rows.anchor: وقال الضحاك : عشرون

rows.speaker: ابن قتيبة
rows.claim: Ibn Qutayba says it is thirty-eight years.
rows.anchor: وحكى ابن قتيبة أنه ثمان وثلاثون

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Ḥasan says forty years, the commonly reported age when bodily growth stops; an unattributed poem urges restraint by forty.
rows.anchor: وقال الحسن : أربعون والمشهور أن الإنسان يقف جسمه عن النمو إذا بلغ ذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The cited poem says a man who reaches forty without modesty or restraint should be left to the course of his life.
rows.anchor: ولذا قيل : إذا المرء وفى الأربعين ولم يكن له دون ما يهوى حياء ولا ستر

rows.speaker: سيبويه
rows.claim: Sībawayh treats ashudd as a plural of shidda, like niʿma and anʿum; al-Kisāʾī and al-Farrāʾ derive it from shadd, while Abū Ḥātim notes afʿul plurals are feminine.
rows.anchor: وهو عند سيبويه جمع واحده شدة كنعمة وأنعم

rows.speaker: الفراء
rows.claim: Al-Farrāʾ says Basrans regard ashudd as a rare-pattern singular; Abū ʿUbayda is also reported to say it has no same-form singular in Arabic.
rows.anchor: وقال الفراء : أهل البصرة يزعمون أنه اسم واحد لكنه على بناء ندر من المفردات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ḥukm can mean wisdom: in religious usage, beneficial knowledge confirmed by action, since knowledge without action is worthless and action without knowledge is folly; it can also mean judgment.
rows.anchor: أي حكمة وهي في لسان الشرع العلم النافع المؤيد بالعمل لأنه بدونه لا يعتد به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ʿIlm means dream interpretation, specified because it is not included in wisdom or because it is especially important and distinctive for Joseph.
rows.anchor: يعني علم تأويل الرؤيا وخص بالذكر لأنه غير داخل فيما قبله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Other interpretations make wisdom prophethood, self-restraint, or judgment among people; knowledge may mean religious or theoretical learning or understanding public interests.
rows.anchor: وفسر بعضهم الحكمة بالنبوة والعلم بالتفقه في الدين وقيل : الحكمة حبس النفس عن هواها

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās interprets the gift as prophethood and sacred law; the indefinite nouns magnify their immeasurable greatness.
rows.anchor: وعن ابن عباس أن الحكم النبوة والعلم الشريعة وتنكيرهما للتفخيم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Interpreting knowledge as dream interpretation strains the reward clause: prison dreams were followed by years in prison, though the king's dream came at hardship's end and could count as reward.
rows.anchor: وتعقب كون المراد بالعلم العلم بتأويل الأحاديث بأن قوله سبحانه : ( وكذلك ( أي مثل ذلك الجزاء العجيب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Calling recipients doers of good links their reward to their excellence and shows God granted Joseph his gifts because he acted well from early on.
rows.anchor: وفي تعليق الجزاء المذكور بالمحسنين إشعار بعلية الإحسان له وتنبيه على أنه تعالى إنما آتاه

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Ḥasan says whoever worships God well in youth is given wisdom by God in maturity.
rows.anchor: ومن هنا قال الحسن : من أحسن عبادة الله سبحانه في شبيبته آتاه الله تعالى الحكمة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A difficulty arises if wisdom is knowledge perfected through action, since good action would then depend on the knowledge supposedly caused by it; action may instead arise through imitation, divine aid, or duties known without revelation.
rows.anchor: واستشكل ما أفاده تعليق الحكم بالمشتق من العلية على تقدير أن يراد من الحكمة العلم المؤيد بالعمل

rows.speaker: بعض المحققين
rows.claim: Some careful scholars say these are different kinds of knowledge, as in the saying that whoever acts on what he knows will be taught what he does not know.
rows.anchor: وقال بعض المحققين : الظاهر تغاير العلمين كما في الأثر من عمل بما علم يسر الله تعالى له

rows.speaker: الضحاك
rows.claim: Al-Ḍaḥḥāk interprets the doers of good as people who patiently endure calamities.
rows.anchor: وعن الضحاك تفسير ( المحسنين ) بالصابرين على النوائب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The narrative returns to Joseph's experience in the Aziz's house; the intervening establishment passage previews that his trials will end well and that he remained upright.
rows.anchor: رجوع إلى شرح ما جرى عليه عليه السلام في منزل العزيز بعد ما أمر امرأته بإكرام مثواه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Murāwada derives from rāda yarūdu, going back and forth gently to seek something, as a scout seeks pasture and water.
rows.anchor: والمراودة المطالبة برفق من راد يرود إذا ذهب وجاء لطلب شيء ومنه الرائد لطالب الكلأ والماء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The reciprocal form may describe one agent because the other side supplies its cause, as a debtor's delay prompts a lender's demand or illness prompts treatment.
rows.anchor: فإن هذه الأفعال وإن كانت صادرة عن أحد الجانبين لكن لما كانت أسبابها صادرة عن الجانب الآخر جعلت كأنها صادرة عنهما

rows.speaker: شيخ الإسلام
rows.claim: Shaykh al-Islām says a cause may stand for and take the name of its effect, as when an initiating act is named by the response it causes.
rows.anchor: قال شيخ الإسلام : وهذا باب لطيف المسك مبني على اعتبار دقيق تحقيقه أن سبب الشيء يقوم مقامه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Her advances are called reciprocal because Joseph's beauty caused them; expressions for rising to pray or reciting Qur'an likewise name intentions by their results.
rows.anchor: وكذلك مراودتها فيما نحن فيه لجمال يوسف عليه السلام نزل صدورها عن محالها بمنزلة صدور مسبباتها

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī explains rāwadat as coaxing a companion to surrender something he does not wish to release; the author says this reflects contesting back and forth.
rows.anchor: وقال الزمخشري هنا أي فعلت ما يفعل المخادع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase indirectly describes her trying to win his agreement; her name is omitted for discretion or because mentioning it was unpleasant.
rows.anchor: ولهذه النكتة جعل كناية عن التمحل لموافقته إياها والعدول عن التصريح بإسمها للمحافظة على الستر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Calling her the woman whose house Joseph occupied emphasizes her motive and, by his resistance despite her beauty and power, his exceptional chastity.
rows.anchor: وإيراد الموصول دون امرأة العزيز مع أنه أخصر وأظهر لتقرير المراودة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Arabs attribute houses to women because they manage or inhabit them, as in the command for the Prophet's wives to stay in their houses.
rows.anchor: لما أن العرب تضيف البيوت إلى النساء باعتبار أنهن القائمات بمصالحه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase woman of the house and a poet's address yā rabbata al-bayt illustrate this usage.
rows.anchor: وكثر في كلامهم صاحبة البيت وربة البيت للمرأة ومن ذلك ياربة البيت قومي غير صاغة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ghallaqat al-abwāb means she closed the house's doors; the intensive form may reflect many doors or repeated closures, with door sections or repeated acts expressed as plural.
rows.anchor: وتشديد الفعل للتكثير في المفعول إن قلنا إن الأبواب كانت سبعة كما قيل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An unnamed view says she closed only two doors: the house entrance and their room.
rows.anchor: وزعم بعضهم أنه لم يغلق إلا بابان باب الدار وباب الحجر التي هما فيها

rows.speaker: الكسائي والفراء
rows.claim: Al-Kisāʾī and al-Farrāʾ gloss hait as come here and say it is a Ḥawrānian word adopted in the Hijaz; Abū Zayd says Hebrew, Ibn ʿAbbās and al-Ḥasan Syriac, and al-Suddī Coptic.
rows.anchor: وفسرها الكسائي والفراء بتعال وزعما أنها كلمة حورانية وقعت إلى أهل الحجاز

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujāhid and others say hait is Arabic, an urging invitation to come to her; the lām explains an omitted phrase such as my desire is for you.
rows.anchor: وقال مجاهد وغيره هي عربية تدعوه لها إلى نفسها وهي كلمة حث وإقبال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another analysis treats hait as a reportative particle meaning I am ready for you, with lām attached, or explains the lām through an omitted expression; tā is part of the word, not a first-person pronoun.
rows.anchor: وجوز كونها اسم فعل خبري كهيهات واللام متعلقة بها والمعنى تهيأت لك

rows.speaker: ابن كثير وأهل مكة
rows.claim: Ibn Kathīr and the Meccan readers read hāʾ open, yāʾ still, and tāʾ with ḍamma; Abū al-Aswad, Ibn Abī Isḥāq, Ibn Muḥayṣin, ʿĪsā, and Ibn ʿAbbās are reported with kasra tāʾ.
rows.anchor: وقرأ ابن كثير وأهل مكة ( هيت ) بفتح الهاء وسكون الياء وضم التاء

rows.speaker: نافع وابن عامر وابن ذكوان والأعرج وشيبة وأبو جعفر
rows.claim: These readers pronounce hāʾ with kasra, yāʾ still, and tāʾ open; al-Ḥalwānī reports Hishām similarly but with hamza.
rows.anchor: وقرأ نافع وابن عامر وابن ذكوان والأعرج وشيبة وأبو جعفر ( هيت ) بكسر الهاء

rows.speaker: الداني وأبو علي الفارسي
rows.claim: Al-Dānī, following Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī, calls the open-tāʾ form a narrator's mistake because it would mean she prepared herself, contrary to the story.
rows.anchor: وتعقب ذلك الداني تبعا لأبي علي الفارسي في الحجة وقد تبعه أيضا جماعة بأن فتح التاء

rows.speaker: صاحب النشر
rows.claim: The author of al-Nashr defends the reading: it can mean your affair is prepared for me or you are made beautiful for me; Hishām's report is sound through several routes.
rows.anchor: ورد ذلك صاحب النشر بأن المعنى على ذلك تهيأ لي أمرك لأنها لم يتيسر لها الخلوة به قبل

rows.speaker: ابن عباس وابن عامر وأبو عمرو
rows.claim: A kasra-hāʾ, hamzated, ḍamma-tāʾ form is reported from these authorities and read by Abū Rajāʾ, Abū Wāʾil, ʿIkrima, Mujāhid, Qatāda, Ṭalḥa, and others; Zayd ibn ʿAlī and Ibn Abī Isḥāq soften its hamza.
rows.anchor: وروي عنه أيضا أنه قرأ بكسر الهاء والهمز وضم التاء وهي رواية أيضا عن ابن عباس

rows.speaker: النحاس
rows.claim: Al-Naḥḥās records a kasra-tāʾ variant and hiyāʾ forms with doubled yāʾ and either fatḥa or kasra on hāʾ.
rows.anchor: وذكر النحاس أنه قريء بكسر الهاء بعدها ياء ساكنة وكسر التاء وقريء أيضا هيا

rows.speaker: ابن هشام
rows.claim: Ibn Hishām calls hiyāʾ a dialect form of hait.
rows.anchor: قال ابن هشام : لغة في ( هيت )

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some say all readings are dialect forms of an imperative noun meaning come here, with tāʾ integral to the word; another view allows a finite verb only with ḍamma tāʾ, with or without hamza.
rows.anchor: وقال بعضهم : إن القراآت كلها لغات وهي فيها إسم فعل بمعنى هلم

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās is also reported to read hayyitu, a passive verb meaning someone prepared her for Joseph.
rows.anchor: ونقل عن ابن عباس أيضا أنه قرأ هييت مثل حببت وهي في ذلك فعل مبني للمفعول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Maʿādh Allāh is a verbal noun meaning I seek refuge in God from what she wants; Joseph rejects the request as an appalling wrong requiring divine protection.
rows.anchor: ( قال معاذ الله ( نصب على المصدر يقال : عذت عوذا وعياذا وعياذة ومعاذا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Inna-hu rabbī refers to her master, the Aziz, who treated Joseph well; this tactfully reminds her that betrayal of his household would be wrong, and the pronoun of the matter emphasizes the statement.
rows.anchor: أي هو ربي أي سيدي العزيز أحسن تعهدي حيث أمرك بإكرامي على أكمل وجه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A later grammarian argues the intensive verb is merely causative because the simple form is poor Arabic; the author says causation and repetition can coexist and the marginal critic misread al-Jawharī.
rows.anchor: وادعى بعض المتأخرين أن التشديد للتعدية وأن كونه للتكثير وهم معللا ذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The poor usage refers to the triliteral verb, not a required intransitive form; the intensive form remains apt. Al-Jawharī explicitly says it marks repetition.
rows.anchor: لأن الرديء الذي ذكره اللغويون إنما هو إستعمال الثلاثي منه لا أن له ثلاثيا لازما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An objection says using rabb for anyone besides God is problematic: creator would be false, while Joseph was himself the Aziz's property if master is meant.
rows.anchor: وتعقب بأن فيه إطلاق الرب على غيره تعالى فإن أريد به الرب بمعنى الخالق فهو باطل

rows.speaker: البحر
rows.claim: Al-Baḥr makes rabb refer to God, who honored Joseph by inclining the Aziz to care for him; the syntax permits two predicates or one predicate followed by an explanatory clause.
rows.anchor: إختار في البحر أن الضمير لله تعالى و ( ربي ) خبر إن و ( أحسن مثواي ) خبر ثان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On the divine reading Joseph warns her against God's punishment; the brief statement itself sufficiently signals that the proposed sin is impossible for him.
rows.anchor: وفيه تحذير لها عن عقاب الله تعالى وجوز على تقدير أن يكون الرب بمعنى الخالق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: La yufliḥu al-ẓālimūn gives a second reason for refusal: oppressors do not attain success.
rows.anchor: وقوله تعالى : إنه لا يفلح الظالمون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Falāḥ is attaining one's aim: worldly felicity includes enduring life, wealth, and honor; afterlife felicity comprises permanence, freedom from poverty and humiliation, and knowledge without ignorance.
rows.anchor: والفلاح الظفر وإدراك البغية وذلك ضربان : دنيوي وأخروي فالأول الظفر بالسعادات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Aflaha means entering felicity like aṣbaḥa; success here likely means the afterlife, and oppressors includes anyone who wrongs.
rows.anchor: ومعنى أفلح دخل في الفلاح كأصبح وأخواته ولعل المراد هنا الفلاح الأخروي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This especially includes those who repay kindness with harm and those who disobey God's command.
rows.anchor: فيدخل في ذلك المجازون للإحسان بالإساءة والعصاة لأمر الله تعالى دخولا أوليا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some specify adulterers because they wrong themselves and the person whose spouse they violate.
rows.anchor: وقيل : الزناة لأنهم ظالمون لأنفسهم وللمزني بأهله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Others specify traitors because they wrong themselves and the people they betray.
rows.anchor: وقيل : الخائنون لأنهم ظالمون لأنفسهم أيضا ولمن خانوه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Her ham was a determined intention to have intercourse, whether ham means intent broadly or firm resolve narrowly; she had already begun its preliminaries and may have reached to touch or embrace him.
rows.anchor: والمعنى أنها قصدت المخالطة وعزمت عليها عزما جازما لا يلويها عنه صارف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The emphatic wording counters any thought that she relented after hearing Joseph's warnings.
rows.anchor: والتأكيد لدفع ما عسى يتوهم من إحتمال إقلاعها عما كانت عليه بما في مقالته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Joseph's ham was only a natural human inclination toward her, like a fasting person desiring cold water; it was involuntary and not a chosen or blameworthy intention.
rows.anchor: أي مال إلى مخالطتها بمقتضى الطبيعة البشرية كميل الصائم في اليوم الحار إلى الماء البارد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ham is used of Joseph by rhetorical matching with her ham, not because his inclination resembled her resolve; only her intention is emphasized.
rows.anchor: وإنما عبر عنه بالهم لمجرد وقوعه في صحبة همها في الذكر بطريق المشاكلة لا لشبهه به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The proof was a manifest divine argument showing adultery's utter evil; seeing it means certainty reaching direct witnessing. Others identify it as moral memories or the written ban on approaching adultery.
rows.anchor: أي حجته الباهرة الدالة على كمال قبح الزنا وسوء سبيله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One careful interpretation says Joseph would have followed natural inclination without seeing the proof, but seeing it kept him steadfast; this accepts only an innocent inclination.
rows.anchor: وجواب ( لولا ) محذوف يدل عليه الكلام أي لولا مشاهدته البرهان لجرى على موجب ميله الجبلي

rows.speaker: البحر
rows.claim: Al-Baḥr denies that Joseph had any ham: the proof's presence negates it, as in saying one would have sinned but for God's protection.
rows.anchor: وفي البحر أنه لم يقع منه عليه السلام هم بها ألبتة بل هو منفي لوجود رؤية البرهان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On al-Baḥr's reading, the answer to lawlā is omitted and indicated by what precedes; the conditional does not assert the act.
rows.anchor: إن جواب ( لو لا ) محذوف لدلالة ما قبله عليه كما يقول جمهور البصريين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some grammarians allow a conditional answer to precede lawlā; the author cites the verse about the woman who nearly exposed Moses.
rows.anchor: فقد قال سبحانه : ( إن كادت لتبدي به لو لا أن ربطنا على قلبها )

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author says no early report of Joseph's alleged sinful intention is sound: reports contradict one another, harm even ordinary believers, and require an unsupported omitted answer.
rows.anchor: فالذي نعتقده أنه لم يصح منها شيء عنهم لأنها أقوال متكاذبة يناقض بعضها بعضا

rows.speaker: ابن عطية
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAṭiyya says the sentence ends after her desire and Joseph's ham answers lawlā; the author says this fails in Arabic and against early authorities.
rows.anchor: لقول ابن عطية : إن قول من قال إن الكلام قد تم في قوله تعالى : ( ولقد همت به )

rows.speaker: الواحدي
rows.claim: Al-Wāḥidī says trusted exegetes reported that Joseph had a genuine resolve and sat with her as a man sits with a woman before the proof removed his desire.
rows.anchor: الواحدي فإنه قال في كتاب البسيط : قال المفسرون الموثوقون بعلمهم المرجوع إلى روايتهم

rows.speaker: علي
rows.claim: Abū Jaʿfar al-Bāqir transmits from ʿAlī that she desired Joseph and he desired her by intending to loosen his waist-tie.
rows.anchor: قال أبو جعفر الباقر : رضي الله تعالى عنه بإسناده عن علي كرم الله تعالى وجهه أنه قال : طمعت فيه

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: One report from Ibn ʿAbbās says Joseph loosened his belt and sat between her legs; another says she lifted him and sat between his thighs as he removed his clothes.
rows.anchor: وعن ابن عباس أنه حل الهميان وجلس منها مجلس الخاتن

rows.speaker: علي
rows.claim: Abū Nuʿaym's Ḥilya report says the proof was Joseph's rebuke when she covered an idol out of modesty: he said he should be more ashamed before God, who sees every soul.
rows.anchor: أبو نعيم في الحلية عن علي كرم الله تعالى وجهه أنها قامت إلى صنم

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Jarīr and others transmit from Ibn ʿAbbās that Jacob appeared to Joseph and struck him on the chest.
rows.anchor: ومنها ما أخرجه ابن جرير وغيره عن ابن عباس أنه عليه السلام مثل له يعقوب عليه السلام

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatāda says Jacob appeared biting his fingers, warning Joseph not to do a fool's act when he was written among prophets.
rows.anchor: ومنها ما أخرجه عن قتادة أنه قال : ذكر لنا أنه مثل له يعقوب عاضا على إصبعيه

rows.speaker: القاسم بن أبي بزة
rows.claim: Al-Qāsim ibn Abī Bazza reports that a voice warned Joseph not to be a feathered bird stripped of feathers by sin; he ignored it until seeing Jacob, then fled in shame.
rows.anchor: ومنها ما أخرجه عن القاسم بن أبي بزة قال : نودي يا ابن يعقوب لا تكونن كالطير له ريش

rows.speaker: الإمام الرازي
rows.claim: Al-Rāzī rejects the alleged sexual sin as an abomination even for a wicked person; God's testimony that He turned evil and obscenity away from Joseph rules it out.
rows.anchor: وتعقب الإمام الرازي ما ذكر بأن هذه المعصية التي نسبوها إلى يوسف وحاشاه من أقبح المعاصي

rows.speaker: الإمام الرازي
rows.claim: If Joseph committed the sin, God's ensuing praise for turning evil and obscenity away from him would be inconsistent with divine wisdom; prophets who err repent, and no repentance is reported here.
rows.anchor: لكان تعقيب ذلك بقوله تعالى : ( كذلك لنصرف عنه السوء والفحشاء ) خارجا عن الحكمة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Joseph's description as one of God's purified servants proves his innocence; Iblīs himself acknowledged he could not mislead God's sincere servants.
rows.anchor: ومن نظر في قوله سبحانه : ( إنه من عبادنا المخلصين ) رآه أفصح شاهد على براءته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author sarcastically challenges detractors to accept either God's testimony of Joseph's purity or Iblīs's admission that he could not mislead the purified.
rows.anchor: إن كانوا من أتباع الله سبحانه فليقبلوا شهادة الله تعالى على طهارته

rows.speaker: الحريري
rows.claim: Al-Ḥarīrī's verse jokes that the speaker began as one of Iblīs's troops but became so vicious that Iblīs became his soldier.
rows.anchor: كما قال الحريري : وكنت امرءا من جند إبليس فانتهى بي الحال حتى صار إبليس من جندي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author says al-Wāḥidī and his supporters have no argument beyond bravado and listing exegetes; the reports are worthless.
rows.anchor: ومن أمعن النظر في الحجج وأنصف جزم أنه لم يبق في يد الواحدي ومن وافقه إلا مجرد التصلف

rows.speaker: الطيبي
rows.claim: Al-Ṭībī adopts the distinction that the woman's ham was a settled decision, whereas Joseph's was a passing involuntary thought without resolve or consent.
rows.anchor: أن الهم همان : هم ثابت وهو ما كان معه عزم وعقد ورضا مثل هم إمرأة العزيز

rows.speaker: محيي السنة
rows.claim: Muḥyī al-Sunna is cited for the distinction between fixed resolve and a passing thought.
rows.anchor: ما حكاه محي السنة عن بعض أهل الحقائق من أن الهم همان

rows.speaker: الطيبي
rows.claim: Al-Ṭībī says to follow the decisive text and prophetic innocence, not blame narrators; reliable hadith authorities transmit no Prophetic report on this, and most stories come from the People of the Book.
rows.anchor: لأن متابعة النص القاطع وبراءة المعصوم عن تلك الرذيلة وإحالة التقصير على الرواة أولى بالمصير إليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Though al-Ḥākim authenticated some reports, qualified scholars regard his authentication here as unreliable; al-Irshād calls the stories absurd fabrications.
rows.anchor: نعم قد صحح الحاكم بعضا من الروايات التي إستند إليها من نسب تلك الشنيعة إليه عليه السلام

rows.speaker: الإمام الرازي
rows.claim: Al-Rāzī argues that even if Joseph's ham is conceded, its omitted object need not be sexual: he may have intended to push her away, which fits his circumstances.
rows.anchor: إنا سلمنا أن الهم قد حصل إلا أنا نقول : لا بد من إضمار فعل مخصوص

rows.speaker: الإمام الرازي
rows.claim: The conditional still matters on the defensive reading: God showed Joseph that pushing her could cause his death or tear his shirt in a way inviting false accusation, so he fled to preserve evidence.
rows.anchor: فأعلمه هذا المعنى فلا جرم لم يشتغل بدفعها وفر عنها حتى صارت الشهادة حجة له

rows.speaker: الشعراني
rows.claim: Some Sufi authorities also interpret Joseph's ham as intending to repel her; al-Shaʿrānī reports asking his teacher about the verse.
rows.anchor: وإلى تقدير الدفع ذهب بعض السادة الصوفية قدس الله تعالى أسرارهم ففي الجواهر والدرر للشعراني

rows.speaker: الشعراني عن شيخه
rows.claim: Al-Shaʿrānī says his teacher professed not to know the ambiguous ham's meaning; the Akbarian explanation is that she sought to overpower Joseph sexually while he sought to overpower her in self-defense.
rows.anchor: سألت شيخنا عن قوله تعالى : ( ولقد همت به وهم بها ) ما هذا الهم الذي أبهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This reading shares an aim to overpower but gives them opposite purposes; she says she tried him against his will, while the surah never says Joseph tried her sexually.
rows.anchor: فالحق أنها همت به عليه السلام لتقهره على ما أرادته منه وهم بها ليقهرها في الدفع

rows.speaker: الإمام الرازي
rows.claim: Al-Rāzī also allows ham to mean desire, as in common expressions for something one does or does not want; the verse could mean she desired him and he desired her.
rows.anchor: وجوز الإمام أيضا تفسير الهم بالشهوة وذكر أنه مستعمل في اللغة الشائعة

rows.speaker: الإمام الرازي
rows.claim: On this reading Joseph would have acted but for seeing his Lord's proof.
rows.anchor: فمعنى الآية ولقد إشتهته واشتهاها ولو لا أن رأى برهان ربه لفعل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author sees no need for this reading: her sinful desire is unproblematic, and ham in this sense is metaphorical, as al-Sayyid al-Murtaḍā says, not literal.
rows.anchor: والظاهر أن الهم بهذا المعنى مجاز كما نص عليه السيد المرتضي في درره لا حقيقة

rows.speaker: أبو علي الجبائي
rows.claim: Abū ʿAlī al-Jubbāʾī and others adopt this interpretation, also reported from al-Ḥasan.
rows.anchor: وقد ذهب إلى هذا التأويل أبو علي الجبائي وغيره وروي ذلك عن الحسن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author rejects popular narratives and refuses to attribute the alleged obscene act to Joseph after he saw God's proof.
rows.anchor: وبالجملة لا ينبغي التعويل على ما شاع في الأخبار والعدول عما ذهب إليه المحققون الأخيار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Sūʾ may be betraying one's master, while fahshāʾ means adultery because of its obscenity; other views make sūʾ the preliminaries of adultery or any evil.
rows.anchor: قيل : خيانة السيد والفحشآء ( الزنا لأنه مفرط القبح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Grammarians differ on what kadhālika points to: the proof's stabilizing effect, God's actions and decrees, His care, or the proof itself; al-Baḥr prefers the vision or reasoning implied by raʾā.
rows.anchor: والكاف على ما قيل : في محل نصب والإشارة إلى التثبيت اللازم للإراءة

rows.speaker: ابن عطية
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAṭiyya attaches the kāf to an implicit statement about God's acts and decrees; Abū al-Baqāʾ and al-Ḥawfī suggest other estimates.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن عطية : إن الكاف متعلقة بمضمر تقديره جرت أفعالنا وأقدارنا

rows.speaker: البحر
rows.claim: Al-Baḥr points the reference to the vision or thought implied by raʾā; a poem shows raʾy can mean literal sight as well as judgment.
rows.anchor: واختار في البحر كون الإشارة إلى الرؤيا المفهومة من رأي أو الرأي المفهوم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A cited poem uses raʾā ʿaynī to attest that raʾy can refer to seeing with the eyes.
rows.anchor: كما في قوله : ورأى عيني الفتى أباكا يعطي الجزيل فعليك ذاكا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author dismisses attaching the prepositional phrase to ham through fronting and inversion; the verse's wording rejects accusations against Joseph.
rows.anchor: ومما لا ينبغي أن يلتفت إليه ما قيل : إن الجار والمجرور متعلق بهم وفي الكلام تقديم وتأخير

rows.speaker: الأعمش
rows.claim: Al-Aʿmash reads liyuṣrifa with third-person yāʾ, explicitly attributing the turning away to the Lord.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الأعمش ليصرف بياء الغيبة وإسناد الصرف إلى ضمير الرب سبحانه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The closing statement that Joseph was one of God's purified servants seals the account of his innocence.
rows.anchor: إنه من عبادنا المخلصين
